world.title: US flight chaos: Nearly 500 departures disrupted, thousands stranded as FAA halts take-offs nationwide; what we know so far
world.summary: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) implemented a nationwide ground stop, causing significant disruptions in air travel across the United States. Nearly 500 flight departures were affected, leaving thousands of passengers stranded. The FAA cited "extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety" as the rationale behind the decision, leading to widespread delays and cancellations throughout the day.

world.title: U.S. flights resume after hours-long outage as FAA lifts nationwide ground stop
world.summary: The FAA lifted a nationwide ground stop on U.S. flights after a major communications outage caused by outdated technology. The grounding lasted several hours on November 13, 2026, leading to significant travel disruptions and confusion across the country. Flights have since resumed, but the incident highlighted vulnerabilities in the aviation communication systems.

world.title: SpaceX's ambitious Starship double-catch attempt fails as booster ends up in Gulf
world.summary: SpaceX's attempt to recover both stages of its Starship rocket in a single mission failed on Friday. The Super Heavy booster, intended to be caught, fell into the Gulf of Mexico instead. This setback highlights the challenges SpaceX faces in its ambitious recovery efforts for the Starship program, which aims to enhance reusability and reduce launch costs.

business.title: Maruti vs M&M vs Hyundai vs Tata Motors PV: Which stock offers growth at a better price?
business.summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles experienced a recovery in Q2 FY27 after addressing operational issues in its UK operations. The launch of new models is expected to drive future growth. Meanwhile, competitors Maruti Suzuki, M&M, and Hyundai Motor India benefited from strong local demand, although rising raw material costs negatively impacted their operating margins.

business.title: SpaceX's ambitious Starship double-catch attempt fails as booster ends up in Gulf
business.summary: SpaceX's attempt to recover both stages of its Starship rocket in a single mission failed on Friday. The Super Heavy booster, intended for recovery, fell into the Gulf of Mexico. This setback marks a significant challenge for SpaceX as it continues to develop its Starship program, which aims to enhance space exploration and transportation capabilities.

business.title: SpaceX's Super Heavy rocket fails catch attempt, malfunctions and explodes on return
business.summary: SpaceX's Super Heavy booster malfunctioned during Starship Flight 15, leading to an automatic abort. The rocket's first stage was diverted to the Gulf of Mexico instead of executing a planned catch at the launch tower. This marked the first recovery attempt for the V3 booster, which ultimately ended in failure as the rocket exploded upon landing offshore.

technology.summary: Quordle offers daily puzzles, with new games released at midnight local time. Players may be engaged with either the current day's puzzle or the previous day's. The article provides hints and answers for Quordle game #1755, dated November 14, and also includes access to past solutions for players seeking assistance with earlier puzzles.

technology.title: 9 tech gifts people will actually use long after Christmas
technology.summary: Nine recommended tech gifts for the holiday season include noise-canceling Bose earbuds, JBL speakers, a sunrise alarm clock from Hatch, and gadgets from DJI. These items were tested throughout the year and are deemed useful long after Christmas. The selections aim to provide practical and enjoyable experiences, making them worthwhile purchases for holiday shoppers.

sports.title: One away from Zaheer Khan! Virat Kohli climbs to second on unwanted list after NZ horror show
sports.summary: Virat Kohli has moved to second place on an unwanted list of Indian cricketers following his duck in the fourth ODI against New Zealand. This performance brings him closer to the record held by former pacer Zaheer Khan. Kohli's dismissal marks a challenging period in his career, as he continues to seek consistency in his batting.

sports.title: Salah seizes Hossam Hassan's African standing: a record Egypt have not achieved in 23 years
sports.summary: Mohamed Salah and the Egypt national football team achieved a significant milestone by matching a scoring record not seen in 23 years. This accomplishment followed a decisive 5-0 victory over South Sudan and another identical win against Malawi at Cairo Stadium during the third round of their matches. The Pharaohs' impressive performance highlights their offensive prowess in recent games.

health.title: Lung cancer prevention in a Changing World: Beyond Tobacco
health.summary: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related deaths globally, posing challenges for healthcare systems. While tobacco use is a well-known risk factor, other contributors to the disease are emerging. Dr. Deepak Abrol emphasizes the need for comprehensive prevention strategies that extend beyond smoking cessation, addressing various environmental and genetic factors influencing lung cancer risk in a changing world.

health.title: Most people dislike coffee at first and learn to love it, and scientists now say the reason may be a slow dopamine signal from the gut that teaches the brain to like flavours linked with calories, eve
health.summary: Research indicates that many people initially dislike coffee but develop a preference over time. Scientists suggest this change may be linked to a slow dopamine signal from the gut, which helps the brain associate flavors with caloric intake. This process explains why individuals often grow to enjoy coffee despite their initial negative reactions to its taste.

science.title: Oceans and forests have absorbed roughly half our carbon emissions for decades, slowing climate change - but can they keep it up?
science.summary: Oceans and forests have absorbed approximately half of human carbon emissions over the past two centuries, mitigating climate change effects. However, new measurements suggest that the ocean's capacity to continue this absorption may decline in the future. As fossil fuel consumption has increased atmospheric carbon dioxide levels, the sustainability of these natural carbon sinks remains uncertain.

science.title: NASA has opened a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge for US high school and college teams to solve problems like power, habitats and astronaut safety on the moon, and registration runs until 25 Ja
science.summary: NASA has launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge, inviting high school and college teams in the U.S. to address challenges related to establishing a long-term lunar base. Participants will focus on issues such as power systems, habitats, and astronaut safety. Registration for the competition is open until January 25, encouraging innovative solutions for lunar exploration.

science.title: NASA Finds Possible Black Hole Behind Mysterious Repeated Explosions Of Giant Star
science.summary: Astronomers using NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory have identified a possible black hole as the cause of a giant star's repeated brightness fluctuations. The study, published in The Astrophysical Journal, reveals that a hidden companion is pulling material from the star at regular intervals, leading to the observed cycles of brightness and dimming. This discovery enhances understanding of stellar interactions.
